nodes.title: How to use
widgets_values:
# Ideogram 4 · FULL · Generate

Choose matching conditional/unconditional weights, Qwen3-VL 8B image encoder and Flux2 VAE. Enter your request in Main Prompt, choose size in Resolution, then Queue. The separate Qwen3-VL 4B enhancer is required for Enhanced; Original skips it.

20 steps, CFG 7, Euler; native resolution-dependent sigmas and late CFG 3 from 70%. Negative text is unused. LoRA starts empty; use compatible weights. Manual and Wildcard share the same enhancer path. Grid is bypassed by default.

## Two independent controls
**Prompt enhancer: Original / Enhanced** controls the description. Enhanced (default) uses the local Qwen3-VL 4B model to fill the scene, style, background and object descriptions. Balanced and High detail are editable. Check Selected prompt and Final Prompt Preview before trusting the result. Styles and exact LoRA triggers are applied afterwards. Original skips the enhancer; for this path, paste a complete Ideogram caption. Plain text is accepted for compatibility but produces a minimal structure and may give gray placeholders.

**Powder Sampler > Ideogram sampling** controls sampling. Standard (default) keeps the existing native schedule. First sigma +0.005 (experimental) changes only the first sampled sigma and keeps the step count. It can help with gray placeholders but can also change composition, contrast or details. It does not disable the enhancer or alter model weights. Use a fixed seed to compare the two modes. No setting guarantees a correct image. Restart ComfyUI after updating to see this control.

## Canvas Layout
Open the Layout tab in Powder Canvas. Match generation size, describe the scene and regions, then enable Use layout. The layout connection is already wired. Layout is off by default. Object boxes are composition annotations, not visible frames. AI descriptions preserve every box and literal text; AI layout proposes a new composition for review. For cropped inpainting the layout must match the crop; disable layout when reusing an unrelated composition. MOSS exports actual-size centered pixel coordinates; Ideogram exports normalized 0-1000 coordinates. Your editor document is saved inside the workflow.

nodes.title: Enhancer instructions · Balanced
widgets_values:
Convert the user's request into a complete Ideogram 4 caption. Return exactly one valid JSON object, without Markdown fences, commentary or reasoning. Use English for descriptions, but preserve explicitly requested visible lettering verbatim in its original language. A subject's name is not a request to print it.

Preserve subjects, species, counts, actions, object states (for example a closed book), colors, materials, relationships, viewpoint, medium and exclusions. Do not add people, animals, props, signatures, logos or visible text that were not requested. Do not turn excluded objects into positive elements. Keep a plain background plain. Do not invent fog, haze, blur or dramatic lighting. Do not render JSON keys, coordinates, annotation boxes, interface graphics or placeholder messages as scene content.

Use exactly these three top-level keys, in this order:
1. high_level_description: a coherent description of the complete requested image. Retain the user's specific constraints rather than replacing them with generic quality words.
2. style_description: fill each field with a concrete description. For photographs, order the keys aesthetics, lighting, photo, medium. The photo field describes only the requested framing and viewpoint. Do not add shallow depth of field, focus blur, lens length or camera settings unless the user explicitly requested them. For artwork, use aesthetics, lighting, medium, art_style instead; do not add photographic lenses or optics to a painting. Respect a specified medium. If none is given, this template defaults to natural photography with restrained lighting. Describe neutral lighting when unspecified, without inventing a new setting.
3. compositional_deconstruction: order its keys background, elements. Describe the requested setting in background; if none is specified, use an unobtrusive unspecified setting without adding named objects. Fill elements with the requested main subjects and relevant supporting objects. Each object has keys type ("obj"), desc. Bounding boxes are optional; do not invent coordinates for ordinary text requests. Describe its visible appearance and state, including important constraints such as closed/open, full body, or exact count. Give distinct foreground objects separate entries: an object held by a person is separate from that person, and a supporting table or pedestal is separate from the object on it. Describe each once, without splitting a single person or animal into duplicate subjects. A scene with several distinct objects must not be collapsed into one all-encompassing element. Preserve states such as a closed book in both its own desc and high_level_description. Background vegetation may stay in background instead of becoming many repeated trees.

For ordinary text requests, describe spatial relationships in words and omit bbox. Only preserve bbox arrays already explicitly provided in an input JSON caption; use their existing [ymin,xmin,ymax,xmax] coordinates without guessing replacements. Every explicitly requested visible text element uses keys type ("text"), text, desc. Preserve supplied bbox if present, placing it after type. Keep lettering exact and describe its requested surface; do not invent additional wording. Include desc for text too.

For an existing JSON caption, preserve its objects, literal text and coordinates; only clarify or fill incomplete descriptions. Never replace its content with an unrelated example. Before returning, check valid JSON escaping, consistent object counts and states, filled style fields, a background description, and concrete elements for the requested subjects. Do not leave empty strings or placeholder descriptions where the request provides content.

BALANCED: keep descriptions concise while retaining all requested details. Use only as many object entries as the scene needs.

Output shape examples follow. These demonstrate format ONLY: use the user's subjects, not the example subjects. Generate one continuous image unless the user explicitly asks for panels or a collage. Do not add bbox coordinates to ordinary text requests.
Photography example:
{"high_level_description": "A product photograph of one white ceramic vase beside one orange on a stone plinth against a plain beige wall.", "style_description": {"aesthetics": "simple product photography", "lighting": "soft even illumination", "photo": "one continuous scene, both objects fully visible", "medium": "photograph"}, "compositional_deconstruction": {"background": "A plain beige wall behind a stone plinth.", "elements": [{"type": "obj", "desc": "One white ceramic vase on the left side of the plinth."}, {"type": "obj", "desc": "One orange beside the vase on the right."}, {"type": "obj", "desc": "The stone plinth supporting both objects."}]}}
Artwork example (notice art_style and the absence of photo):
{"high_level_description": "A gouache painting of one sailboat on a lake, reeds in the foreground and a distant shoreline. A single continuous landscape on paper.", "style_description": {"aesthetics": "opaque gouache brushwork on paper", "lighting": "soft daylight", "medium": "painting", "art_style": "traditional gouache landscape"}, "compositional_deconstruction": {"background": "A distant shoreline behind the lake, within the same continuous landscape.", "elements": [{"type": "obj", "desc": "One sailboat in the middle distance on the lake."}, {"type": "obj", "desc": "The lake surface extending into the foreground around the boat."}, {"type": "obj", "desc": "Reeds at the lower left edge of the lake."}]}}
Now return only the caption for the user's request. For watercolor, gouache, drawing, illustration or other artwork, use art_style, NOT photo. Keep the requested image as one coherent scene. Do not copy example objects or add any extra image panels.
